value.module: pricing.py loads data_pricing/ relative to the module file; no tax logic

why: Team standard: money as float dollars, percents as fractions, lookup miss = None. Customer region is a plain code (e.g. TX) so tax.py can key on it. Discount is stored as a rate; applying it and rounding is left to invoice.py.

value: tax.compute_tax(region, discount_pct, lines) -> {"tax_pct": number, "taxable_base_cents": int, "tax_cents": int}; region: str (e.g. "TX") or None for unknown customer; discount_pct: percent number (10 = 10%); lines: list of {"category": str, "amount_cents": int}; all money in integer cents; tax_cents rounded half-up to the cent, computed once from the summed taxable amount.
why: Concrete signature for invoice.py to call. tax.py does all tax math; invoice.py only uses the returned values. Taxable base = sum of lines whose category is not in exempt_categories.csv; base reduced by discount_pct; tax = base * tax_pct / 100 rounded half-up.

value: region=None -> tax_pct 0 (unknown customer, per RULES.md). A region string not present in rates.csv -> raise KeyError (team standard). Category matching is exact on the stripped string.
why: RULES.md says an unknown customer pays 0%, which conflicts with the team KeyError rule. Resolution: only a missing customer (region None) gets 0%; a non-empty region not in the rates table is a data error and raises KeyError.

value.get_item: get_item(sku: str) -> dict: {"price": Decimal dollars} for a known sku, {} (empty dict) if unknown
value.get_customer: get_customer(cid: str) -> dict: {"name": str, "discount": Decimal multiplier} e.g. 10% off is Decimal("0.90"), no discount is Decimal("1"); {} if unknown

why: Unknown lookups return an empty dict so a price of 0 (free item) is not confused with unknown. Discount is a multiplier per team standard.

value.calculate: calculate(customer_id: str, lines: list of (sku, Decimal line amount before discount), discount_multiplier: Decimal) -> (rate: Decimal multiplier e.g. Decimal("1.0825"), tax: Decimal dollars rounded half-up to cent). tax.py decides taxability per sku. Unknown customer -> (Decimal("1"), Decimal("0.00")). Invoice passes only known skus.

why: tax.py needs sku for taxability and the discount multiplier to get the taxable base. Spec example: full discounted subtotal 35.19 * 8.25% = 2.90, but spec tax is 1.86, so taxability must be per line; tax.py must own that.

Units conflict with the team standard that pricing_api follows: money must be float dollars (not integer cents) and percents must be fractions (discount_rate 0.10, not discount_pct 10). Please propose v2 e.g. compute_tax(region, discount_rate, lines) with lines [{category, amount: float dollars}] and returning {tax_rate: fraction, taxable_base: float dollars, tax: float dollars rounded half-up to the cent}. Pricing has no objection to the category/exempt logic itself.
